newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end flat, stifled by higher bond yields.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end flat, stifled by higher bond yields.

text.p: * New Zealand shares close flat on hefty turnover
* Higher bond yields take shine off firm tone in NZ equities
* All eyes on U.S. non-farm payrolls data tonight
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
306 -1 * NZSC cap index -13.20 at 4,960.42
344 -2 * Volume NZ$89.4 million. Futures +2 at 1,112
657 +1 * Other movers - +3 -15
New Zealand shares closed flat on Friday as higher bond yields began to take the shine off the equity market's firm tone, brokers said.
"You've really got to start scratching your head when you see New Zealand bonds increase in yield...you've really got to say we've got a problem here," said Sean Vaughan at County Natwest.
Bond yields have risen sharply in the last two days, attracting investors' attention away from equities.
"That's probably holding Telecom back. But against that it looks like you've got some reasonably strong inflows of money into our market," Vaughan said.

The NZSE-40 Capital Index finished Friday's session 0.38 of a point down at 2,225.53, with Telecom the only leader to post a gain, up a cent at NZ$6.57. The top-40 index had been in positive territory for most of the day.
"You've got the new quarter this week and it seems to be that more money is flowing into international markets such as ours. People obviously believe there is still value here," Vaughan said.

Brokers said crossings prior to the open helped to boost overall turnover, for example a line of five million Progressive shares. The supermarket chain, 58 percent owned by Foodland closed three cents stronger at NZ$1.48.
Brierley Investments Ltd saw solid two-way business, with 6.2 million shares trading. BIL ended a cent weaker at $1.30.

With the focus on bond yields at present, brokers said all eyes would be on U.S. non-farm payrolls data tonight (NZT) for an indication of which way New Zealand interest rates will move next week. --Matthew Brockett, Wellington Newsroom 64 4 473-3736
